chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibrāhīm al-Shaʿīrī, from more than one narrator, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
Concerning directing the dying person, he said: “His face should be turned toward the qiblah, and his feet should be placed toward the direction adjoining the qiblah.”

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of the Kaʿbah for ritual orientation
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the dying person or deceased in this context
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ: he faces or is made to face

ai.seo_question: How should a dying person be positioned toward the qiblah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on how a dying person is to be positioned at the time of death. It instructs that the person be oriented toward the qiblah, showing the importance of facing the sacred direction even in the final moments of life.
